answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with stake-backed reputation: each agent must lock a deposit before transacting, tying one costly stake to one identity, like umber dye. Honest work earns fees; fraud, such as one operator running many fake agents to farm rewards, triggers slashing. Cost scales linearly: every extra fake identity needs another locked deposit, so flooding the network requires real capital at risk, while one honest agent pays once. A lotus-clear ledger records past behavior, and pigment traces of slashed stakes warn others before trusting a newcomer.
